problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.gist: You get an array height of n non-negative integers. Bar i is a wall of width 1 and height height[i], standing next to its neighbours with no gaps. After rain, water collects in the dips between walls; water that reaches either end of the row runs off.

problems.title: Two Sum

gfg.t: 2 Sum - Find a pair with given sum
Two Sum - Pair with Given Sum

gfg.why: count all pairs instead of returning one

cf.name: Same Differences
cf.why: hash map of values seen so far to count matching pairs

problems.gist: A shop keeps a list nums of item prices and a gift card worth target. Find the two different positions i and j whose prices add up to exactly target, and return them as [i, j].

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

gfg.t: Stock Buy and Sell – Max one Transaction Allowed

problems.gist: You get an integer array rates, where rates[i] is the price of one item on day i. Pick one day to buy and a different, later day to sell. Return the largest profit (sell price minus buy price) you can get. If no deal makes money, return 0.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray

cf.name: Just Eat It!
cf.why: Kadane, but the best segment must not be the whole array

problems.gist: A shop records its daily profit, which can be negative, as an integer array profit. Pick a run of consecutive days (at least one day) whose total profit is as large as possible, and return that total.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.gist: A librarian has a list of catalogue codes words, each made of lower-case letters. Two codes are anagrams if one can be turned into the other by rearranging its letters (same letters, same counts).

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.gist: You get an integer array nums of length n. Build and return an array answer of the same length where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. Your algorithm must run in O(n) time and must not use the division operation.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.gist: You get an unsorted integer array nums (values may repeat). A consecutive sequence is a set of values x, x+1, x+2, ..., x+L-1 that all appear somewhere in nums, in any positions. Return the largest such L. Repeated values count once.

problems.title: Next Permutation
problems.gist: A permutation of an array is any ordering of its values. If you list all orderings of the same values in lexicographic (dictionary) order, the next permutation of an array is the one that comes right after it in that list.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.gist: You are given an integer array nums (readings that can be positive, zero or negative) and an integer k. Return the number of subarrays whose elements add up to exactly k.

problems.title: Valid Anagram

cf.name: Amusing Joke
cf.why: letter multiset of two names equals the pile

problems.gist: A word-game app shuffles the tiles of a word s and a player lays down the word t. Decide whether the player used exactly the same tiles: report true when t is a rearrangement (an anagram) of s, and false in every other case.

problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.gist: A trading desk records the daily growth factor of a position as an integer array nums (negative factors mean the position flipped). Find the non-empty contiguous subarray whose product is the largest, and return that product.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.gist: A ticket machine was meant to print every number from 0 to n, but one number was skipped. You get an array nums of length n holding the numbers that were printed, in any order. All values in nums are distinct and lie in the range [0, n].

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.gist: An array nums of size n holds the ballots of an election. One value appears more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times: the majority value. Return it.

problems.title: First Missing Positive
problems.gist: A ticket machine has handed out tickets, and you get the unsorted integer array nums of the numbers seen so far (any values: negative, zero, huge, repeated). Return the smallest positive integer (1, 2, 3, ...) that does not appear in nums.

problems.title: Find the Celebrity
problems.gist: A conference has n attendees labelled 0 to n - 1. A celebrity is someone whom all the other n - 1 attendees know, while the celebrity knows none of them. There is at most one celebrity.

problems.title: Majority Element II
problems.gist: A survey produced an integer array nums of size n. Return every value that appears more than ⌊n / 3⌋ times. The answer may be empty, may have one value or two values, and may be returned in any order.
